issues.location: the screenshot shows a bot-protection interstitial rather than real site content... the screenshot shows a bot-protection interstitial rather than an actual product detail page... the screenshot shows a bot-protection interstitial rather than the actual product listing page
issues.explanation: The report acknowledges three times that screenshots show Cloudflare WAF challenge pages rather than actual site content, yet these screenshots are included in the diagnostic pipeline output and referenced as part of the analysis. WAF/bot-protection interstitials must not be presented as or alongside real site content captures without clear disqualification from the analysis.

issues.location: Unique, keyword-targeted product descriptions can increase organic traffic per PDP by 30-50% (Ahrefs)
issues.explanation: The claim that unique product descriptions increase organic traffic by 30-50%, attributed to Ahrefs, is a debunked fabricated benchmark. Ahrefs has never published this statistic. It appears twice in the report (sections 2 and 4) and once in the references section.

issues.location: Products with 50+ reviews convert at 2-3x versus products with no reviews (Bazaarvoice / Spiegel Research Center)
issues.explanation: This is a misrepresentation of the Spiegel Research Center finding. The actual stat is that 5 reviews (not 50+) produce a 270% conversion lift. The '50+ reviews at 2-3x' framing is a debunked fabricated benchmark, regardless of attribution.

issues.location: Product recommendations drive 10-30% of e-commerce revenue (McKinsey)
issues.explanation: This is a well-documented fabricated benchmark. McKinsey never published a stat claiming product recommendations drive 10-30% of e-commerce revenue. This figure has been debunked and should not be cited.

issues.location: average AOV uplift with cross-sell is 8-15% (Baymard Institute)
issues.explanation: Baymard Institute has never published an AOV uplift figure of 8-15% for cross-sell. This is a fabricated benchmark incorrectly attributed to Baymard, whose research focuses on usability and checkout UX, not revenue lift metrics.

issues.location: Rich snippets increase CTR by 20-40% (Search Engine Journal / Ahrefs)
issues.explanation: Search Engine Journal is a generic industry blog, not a peer-reviewed or primary research source. Citing it alongside Ahrefs as a co-source for a business intelligence benchmark does not meet the standard for credible industry data. Generic blog posts are flagged as weak sources.

issues.location: Companies with active blogs generate approximately 55% more visitors (HubSpot)
issues.explanation: HubSpot is a vendor with commercial interest in content marketing adoption. Their self-published blog statistics are frequently cited as industry benchmarks but originate from HubSpot's own customer base surveys and marketing materials, qualifying as a generic/vendor blog source rather than independent research.

summary: The report contains four separate fabricated benchmarks (Ahrefs 30-50% traffic uplift, Spiegel 50+ reviews, McKinsey 10-30% revenue from recommendations, Baymard 8-15% AOV uplift), one WAF screenshot transparency issue, and two weak source citations, making it unreliable for client delivery without significant benchmark revision.
